title: CHAPTER THIRTEEN. On the mode and necessary consequence and end of the resurrection — namely the last judgment
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): 4:15). 1 Thess. 15:51; 6–7: gathering belonging toward dust, formation belonging toward ye body, animation — but it stands as a mystery (1 Cor. 12 aph. The mode can be reduced to ye form explained in Cap. The mode belonging toward ye resurrection stands as not perfectly known — he who willed such that not even belonging toward all natural things ye modes plus reasons be open to us. II. || now follow its mode plus necessary consequence plus end. So far have been ye causes belonging toward ye resurrection; || On ye mode plus necessary consequence plus end belonging toward ye resurrection — namely ye last judgment. Caput ye thirteenth.
pass_b_english: CHAPTER THIRTEEN. On the mode and necessary consequence and end of the resurrection — namely the last judgment.
So far have been the causes of the resurrection; now follow its mode and necessary consequence and end.

II. The mode of the resurrection is not perfectly known — he who willed that not even of all natural things the modes and reasons be open to us. The mode can be reduced to the form explained in Cap. 12 aph. 6–7: gathering of dust, formation of the body, animation — but it is a mystery (1 Cor. 15:51; 1 Thess. 4:15).
source_text: CAPUT DECIMUM TERTIUM. De modo & necessario consequente atque fine resurrectionis, nimirum ultimo judicio. Hactenus fuerunt resurrectionis causae; jam sequitur ejus modus & necessarium consequens atque finis. II. Modus resurrectionis non perfecte cognitus est, qui ne naturalium quidem rerum omnium modos & rationes nobis apertas esse voluit. Modus ad formam cap. 12. aph. 6 & 7 explicatam reduci potest: collectio pulverum, formatio corporis, animatio — sed mysterium est, 1 Cor. 15.51 & 1 Thess. 4.15.
